items.definition:
hawker, street vendor
A peddler was selling trinkets by the roadside.

a sound unit, a method of teaching reading
Children learn to read using phonics to understand letter sounds.

a soft, wet sound
We heard the plop of a pebble as it fell into the water.

a new evaluation
The project requires a complete reassessment of its goals and budget.

a person who registers
Each registrant received a welcome packet at the conference.

a weight used to sink a fishing line or net; a type of baseball pitch
He attached a lead sinker to his fishing line.

a person who is irritating because they think they know everything
Don't be such a smartass and just answer the question.

a sudden, intense burst of light or energy; a type of candy
The fireworks created a beautiful starburst in the night sky.

a small statue
She placed the delicate statuette on the mantelpiece.

a large gulp of a drink
He took a big swig of water from the bottle.

a mustache (informal, British English)
He grew a big bushy tash for Movember.

a large muscle on the back of the upper arm
He felt a strain in his tricep after lifting weights.

a vice president (informal)
The veep gave a speech at the conference.

the state of being wet
The wetness of the grass soaked his shoes.

a slight involuntary grimace or shrinking movement
He gave a slight wince as the needle went in.

the process of making wine
Winemaking is a complex art and science.

a person or thing that destroys or causes ruin
The storm was a wrecker of homes along the coast.

a safeguard or fallback arrangement
The agreement included a backstop to prevent a hard border.

a large, strong person, especially one who is aggressive
He was a big bruiser, but surprisingly gentle.

a person who carries a golfer's clubs
The golfer thanked his caddie after the game.

a pupa of a butterfly or moth
The caterpillar transformed into a chrysalis.

a secret name for a person, place, or thing
The new project was given the codename 'Phoenix'.

a person who founds something with another or others
She is the cofounder of a successful tech startup.

the act of putting something off to a later time
The student requested a deferral of his admission.

a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun
Scientists have discovered thousands of exoplanets.

a ballroom dance
They learned to dance the foxtrot at the studio.

a blow with the head
He gave his opponent a headbutt during the fight.

a person who interrupts a speaker with taunts or questions
The comedian was interrupted by a heckler in the audience.

a young female cow that has not borne a calf
The farmer bought a new heifer for his herd.

deceptive or false talk or behavior
He dismissed the whole idea as a complete humbug.

the ability of a computer or other device to respond to a user's actions
The new software offers enhanced interactivity.

a short excursion or journey for pleasure
They took a short jaunt to the countryside.

printed stationery
The official letter was printed on company letterhead.

a period of one thousand years
The new millennium brought significant technological advancements.

a wrong step or a mistake
One misstep could cost them the entire competition.

the quality of being new
The newness of the car quickly wore off.

panels, especially wooden ones, used to decorate a wall
The old library had dark wooden paneling on the walls.

pectoral muscle
He worked out his chest, focusing on his pec muscles.

a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation
She found herself in a quandary, unsure of which path to take.

a person or company that refines a substance
The oil refiner processes crude oil into various petroleum products.

an imitation diamond made from rock crystal or glass
Her dress was adorned with sparkling rhinestones.

back of the neck
The mother cat carried her kitten by the scruff of its neck.

the quality of being sexy
Her confidence added to her overall sexiness.

bundle (of grain or papers)
The farmer gathered the wheat into sheaves.

one who sniffs
The police used a sniffer dog to find the hidden drugs.

potato (informal)
We had some crispy fried taters with our dinner.

a dull, heavy sound
The apple fell to the ground with a soft thunk.

the process of forming or joining a labor union
The debate over unionization in the tech industry is growing.

a group of wolves hunting together; a group of submarines operating together
The wolfpack surrounded their prey in the forest.

a long-haired breed of cat or rabbit; yarn made from its hair
She knitted a soft scarf from angora wool.

a device for applying a substance
She used a cotton swab as an applicator for the medicine.

a person who deliberately sets fire to property
The police are searching for the arsonist responsible for the warehouse fire.

a marine crustacean that attaches to surfaces
The ship's hull was covered in barnacles.

various dark-colored fish or small whales
The documentary 'Blackfish' raised concerns about orcas in captivity.

a reddish-brown sandstone; a building faced with this stone
Many historic homes in New York City are brownstones.

a long, loose garment covering the whole body from head to feet, worn in public by some Muslim women
In some regions, women wear a burka in public.

the last car of a freight train
The conductor rode in the caboose at the end of the train.

a hardened part of the skin or soft tissue
Years of playing guitar gave him calluses on his fingertips.

an orange or red pigment found in plants
Carrots are rich in beta-carotene.

a winged angelic being; a beautiful child
The painting depicted a cherub with rosy cheeks.

a person with whom one shares a secret or private matter, trusting them not to repeat it to others
She was her closest friend and confidante.

a short, broad saber with a curved blade, formerly used by sailors
The pirate brandished his cutlass.

a device used to set off an explosive
The bomb squad carefully disarmed the detonator.

a person or company that exterminates pests
We had to call an exterminator to deal with the ant problem.
